COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Maria Mitchell is an astronomer. Maria Mitchell ( mə-RY-ə; August 1, 1818 – June 28, 1889) was an American astronomer, librarian, naturalist, and educator.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Barium?
Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
What is the atomic number of Nickel?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
In what year did J. Robert Oppenheimer die?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year was Mass–energy equivalence discovered?
Mass–energy equivalence: In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Which company manufactures Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: Hawker Siddeley. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
NHIndustries NH90: Airbus Helicopters. The NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
These mostly semiaquatic vertebrates are tetrapods that pointedly lack an amniotic membrane, splitting into just three living orders like the frogs and toads of Anura — what are they?
Amphibian are ectothermic, anamniotic, four-limbed vertebrate animals that constitute the class Amphibia.
Native to Europe but introduced to North America, this orb-weaver spider species is known by several common names, one of them shared confusingly with a different species — which species?
Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.

Thought to be the world's most abundant bird of prey in its family, with an estimated 6.7 million individuals, this opportunistic raptor is known for its angled wings and distinctive forked tail — what is it?
Black kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.
Meaning 'thunder lizard' in Greek, this sauropod dinosaur genus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879 from a partial, skull-less skeleton found in Wyoming's Como Bluff — what dinosaur is it?

Brontosaurus (literally 'thunder lizard', from the Greek words bront, 'thunder', and saros, 'lizard') is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day United States during the Late Jurassic period.
Its name comes from the Latin for "coal," and one of its isotopes decays with a 5,700-year half-life that lets scientists date ancient remains — which element is it?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Along with the bonobo, which great ape of equatorial Africa's forests and savannas is humans' closest living relative, according to DNA and fossil evidence?
Chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.

The first anatomically modern humans known to inhabit Europe and Siberia, arriving as early as 56,800 years ago, this population interbred with the indigenous Neanderthals before the latter went extinct — who are they?
Cro-Magnon (EEMH) were the first early modern humans (Homo sapiens) found in Europe and Siberia, continuously occupying the continent possibly from as early as 56,800 years ago.

Named from the Latin word for 'finger' because of its tubular, spike-borne flowers, this genus of about 20 European and West Asian species was reclassified into a new plant family in 2001 — what is it commonly called?
Digitalis (or) is a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous perennial plants, shrubs, and biennials, commonly called foxgloves.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints, stretchy velvety skin, and abnormal scarring, sometimes leading to aortic dissection — name the condition?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) are a group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders.
From abortion to animal welfare to business practices, the 'applied' branch of this philosophical study tackles real-world moral problems. What is it?
Ethics is the philosophical study of moral phenomena. Its main branches include normative ethics, applied ethics, and metaethics.
Discovered in 1999 at a Dubna lab, this synthetic superheavy element (symbol Fl, number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name was transliterated from Cyrillic — which element?
Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.

The first person in Germany to hold a professorship dedicated to experimental physics, he is remembered for his posthumous 'waste book' notebooks and for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him. Who is he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1 July 1742 - 24 February 1799) was a German physicist, satirist, and Anglophile.

These common coastal seabirds, most closely related to terns and skimmers, were once known by an older name still surviving in some English dialects and cognate with the German word Möwe — what birds are they?
Gull (see Taxonomy), are seabirds of the subfamily Larinae.
First identified in 1910, this organic compound is stored in mast cells and basophils and, though not made by classic endocrine glands, still acts as a local hormone — what compound is it?
Histamine is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.

For decades this University of Virginia psychiatrist ran a Division of Perceptual Studies and gathered evidence that memories — and even bodily features — might carry across lives. Which researcher into reincarnation was he?

Ian Stevenson (October 31, 1918 - February 8, 2007) was a Canadian-born American psychiatrist, the founder and director of the Division of Perceptual Studies at the University of Virginia School of Medicine.

This American physicist worked on the Manhattan Project, then in 1949 proposed that — contrary to belief — not all atomic nuclei are spherical, an idea Aage Bohr later helped confirm. Who won a share of the 1975 Nobel for it?
James Rainwater (December 9, 1917 - May 31, 1986) was an American physicist who shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1975 for his part in determining the asymmetrical shapes of certain atomic nuclei.

The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, this astronaut and aerospace engineer first studied in India before earning advanced degrees in the US and flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 — who was she?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 - February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.

Spread by the bite of sandflies and caused by a genus of protozoal parasites, this tropical disease can present as skin ulcers, disfiguring mucosal damage, or a more dangerous internal form. Name the disease?
Leishmaniasis is a wide array of clinical manifestations caused by protozoal parasites of the Trypanosomatida genus Leishmania.
Named for antennae often longer than its own body, this insect family boasts over 35,000 species and gets its name from a Greek myth about a shepherd transformed after angering nymphs — which group?
Longhorn beetle (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species described.
This computer scientist led the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo Guidance Computer and is credited with coining the very term 'software engineering' — who is she?
Margaret Hamilton (software engineer) (ne Heafield; born August 17, 1936) is an American computer scientist.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.
This Turkish government minister for environment and climate will preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31 — who is he?
Murat Kurum is the minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change in Turkey, and president of the 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31.

A former director of Russia's FSB intelligence agency, this politician served as Secretary of the Security Council of Russia from 2008 to 2024 and is considered one of Putin's closest advisors — who is he?
Nikolai Patrushev (born 11 July 1951) is a Russian politician, security officer and former intelligence officer who served as the secretary of the Security Council of Russia from 2008 to 2024.
Also covering the modification of facial growth known as dentofacial orthopedics, this branch of dentistry corrects mal-positioned teeth and bite patterns. What field is it?

Orthodontics (also referred to as orthodontia) is a dentistry specialty that addresses the diagnosis, prevention, management, and correction of mal-positioned teeth and jaws, as well as misaligned bite patterns.
This species of hickory tree, native to the Mississippi River region of the southern US and northern Mexico, is the official state nut of five states and the state tree of Texas. What nut is this?
Pecan (pih-KAN,; Carya illinoinensis) is a species of hickory native to the Southern United States and northern Mexico in the region of the Mississippi River.
These drifting, self-feeding members of the plankton community photosynthesize like land plants, so they crowd the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.
This chemical compound, known in nature as the mineral niter and historically as a form of saltpetre, is widely used in fertilizers. What is it?
Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
A polyphenol from the flavonoid family with a naturally bitter taste, this compound turns up in capers and red onions and gets added to supplements — what is it?
Quercetin is a plant flavonol from the flavonoid group of polyphenols.
Holding a professorship in biology, neurology, and neurosurgery at Stanford, this primatologist is also a research associate with Kenya's National Museums — who is he?
Robert Sapolsky (born April 6, 1957) is an American academic, neuroscientist, and primatologist.
This group of autoimmune diseases causes patches of thickened skin and poor blood flow to the fingers in cold weather, with one severe subtype called CREST syndrome — what condition is it?
Scleroderma is a group of autoimmune diseases that may result in changes to the skin, blood vessels, muscles, and internal organs.
About 0.01% of people are born with this condition, in which the heart typically ends up on the right side of the chest instead of the left — what is it?
Situs inversus is a congenital condition in which the major visceral organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.
Though some scientists place it in its own genus, Acrocodia, the Malayan species is usually still classified within this genus of tapir — name this genus?
Tapirus is a genus of tapir which contains the living tapir species.
Joining a tech giant in 1998 to run worldwide operations, this executive served as its COO before stepping up to CEO the day Steve Jobs resigned in 2011 — who is he?
Tim Cook (born November 1, 1960) is an American business executive who has served as the chief executive officer (CEO) of Apple since 2011.
Lined with a type of tissue called transitional epithelium, this narrow tube can develop kidney stones or reflux problems and connects each kidney to the bladder — what is it?
Ureter are tubes composed of smooth muscle that transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Commonly called a canker sore, this recurring condition produces benign mouth ulcers that heal within 7 to 10 days but often return three to six times a year — what is it?
Aphthous stomatitis: Common oral condition lasting 7–10 days.
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Also known as the penny bun or porcino, this prized edible fungus can grow a brown cap up to a foot wide and forms symbiotic partnerships with forest tree roots — which mushroom?
Boletus edulis: Species of mushroom, widely distributed in the Northern Hemisphere.
Bred in the 19th century as a guard dog by crossing the English Mastiff with the now-extinct Old English Bulldog, which large, short-muzzled English breed was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1924?
Bullmastiff: English breed of dog. The Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
Designated Alpha Carinae and located some 310 light-years away, this bright giant is the second-brightest star in the night sky, outshone only by Sirius — which star?
Canopus: Brightest star in the constellation of Carina.
A first-generation cephalosporin and β-lactam, this antibiotic can be taken by mouth and treats ear, bone, skin and urinary infections by disrupting bacterial cell-wall growth — what is it?
Cefalexin: Beta-lactam antibiotic. Cefalexin, also spelled cephalexin, is an antibiotic that can treat a number of bacterial infections.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
A group of these black birds is famously called a 'murder,' and their larger cousins are known as ravens — what bird is this?
Crow: Index of animals with the same common name.
The second jet fighter to enter RAF service and the first powered by a single jet engine, this twin-boom aircraft flew with the Halford Goblin turbojet — which aircraft?

De Havilland Vampire: Fighter aircraft; first single-engine jet in RAF service. The de Havilland DH100 Vampire is a British jet fighter developed and manufactured by the de Havilland Aircraft Company.

Previously known as multiple personality condition and popularized (inaccurately) by the case of 'Sybil,' this controversial mental health diagnosis is characterized by the presence of two or more distinct personality states known as 'alters' — which condition is this?
Dissociative identity disorder: Mental illness with multiple personality states.
Its leaves and flowers are covered in dense white hairs that shield it from Alpine cold and UV rays, making this daisy-family flower a symbol of mountaineering purity — what is it?
A sympathomimetic stimulant often used to keep blood pressure up during anesthesia, this drug has also been tried for asthma, narcolepsy, and obesity — what is it?

Ranging from Northern Europe through Siberia to the Himalayas, this medium-sized wild cat is one of only four living species in its genus and can be found at elevations up to 5,500 meters — what animal is this?
Eurasian lynx: Species of medium-sized cat native to Eurasia.

Named for the physicist who reportedly asked 'but where is everybody?' at Los Alamos in 1950, this puzzle questions why we've found no evidence of alien civilizations despite the odds favoring them — what's it called?
Fermi paradox: Discrepancy of the lack of evidence for alien life despite its apparent likelihood.
This American physician-scientist led the Human Genome Project before directing the NIH for over a decade under three presidents — who guided the mapping of our DNA?

Named after a long-nosed, insect-eating African animal, this 1960s supersonic fighter-bomber pioneered variable-sweep wings and automated terrain-following radar under Robert McNamara's TFX program. What aircraft is it?
General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark: Family of strike aircraft developed in 1960s.
Dubbed the 'king of the birds' in European folklore for its golden head crest, this tiny kinglet's scientific name literally means 'petty king' — which bird?
Goldcrest: Small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, which benign condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men?
Gynecomastia: Enlargement of the human male breast.

This French mathematician, famous for his work in algebraic topology, came from an almost absurdly mathematical dynasty: son of mathematician Élie, nephew of mathematician Anna, and brother to a composer, a physicist, and yet another mathematician — who was he?
This small rodent, pointed-snouted with large rounded ears, has become the standard laboratory model organism after thriving alongside human settlements — what is it?

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?

A former Chicago options trader with finance degrees but no PhD, this entrepreneur co-founded a dot-com company whose peer-reviewed project evolved into the world's largest free encyclopedia — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
He served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, ran the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning his professorship there in 2026. Which economist is this?
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

Born into one of Europe's richest families in Vienna, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge before giving away his inheritance and enlisting in the Austro-Hungarian Army — who is he?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Austrian philosopher and logician (1889–1951)
Grown as the source of the tropical mango fruit, this evergreen tree in the cashew family can reach 30 meters tall and comes in two genetic types — what species is it?
Mangifera indica: Species of flowering plant in the cashew family Anacardiaceae.
Combined with formaldehyde to create hardwearing resins found in Formica countertops, plastic dinnerware, and the foam in a Magic Eraser, this nitrogen-rich compound also resists fire — what is it?
Melamine: Fire-resistant chemical used in dinnerware, insulation, and cleaning products.
Often striking one side of the head and sometimes preceded by a sensory 'aura,' this neurological disorder brings nausea and sensitivity to light and sound — what is it?
Migraine: Disorder resulting in recurrent moderate–severe headaches.
Sold under the brand name Singulair, this asthma medication blocks leukotriene D4 in the lungs but received a UK black box warning in 2019 over neuropsychiatric side effects — what is it?
Montelukast: Medication used in asthma or COPD.
This genus of venomous elapid snakes across Africa and Asia is home to the 'true cobras' — after a 2009 taxonomic revision folded in two other genera, it now contains 38 species — which genus?
Naja: Genus of snakes. Until recently, the genus Naja had 20 to 22 species, but it has undergone several taxonomic revisions in recent years, so sources vary greatly.
Colourless and odourless, this element pairs with itself to form a diatomic gas that makes up about 78% of the air you're breathing — what is it?
Nitrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 7 (N)
Named after the Greek word for tumor, first used this way by the physician Galen nearly two millennia ago, this medical field focuses on diagnosing and treating cancer — what is it called?
Oncology: Branch of medicine dealing with, or specializing in, cancer.
This condition inflames a large organ behind the stomach, sending severe upper-abdominal pain into the back, with chronic cases bringing weight loss and fatty stool — what is it?
Almost every member of this flightless, countershaded clan sticks to the Southern Hemisphere — except one lone species that creeps up to the equator in the Galapagos. What bird is it?
Penguin: Family of aquatic flightless birds.
Whether captured chemically on light-sensitive film or electronically by an image sensor, this art is fundamentally the practice of recording light — what is it?
Photography: Art and practice of creating images by recording light.
Whether natural silk or synthetic nylon, this class of polymer is defined by repeating units joined through amide bonds — what is it?
Polyamide: Macromolecule with repeating units linked by amide bonds.

Native to western Eurasia and a member of the rose family, this species — the wild or sweet cherry — is the ancestor of the sour cherry, though every part of the plant except its ripe fruit is mildly toxic. What is it called?
Prunus avium: Species of flowering plant in the rose family. The species is often cultivated as an ornamental tree.
Also known as hexogen, this nitroamine explosive is the key energetic agent in C-4 and a core ingredient of Semtex — which compound?
RDX: Explosive chemical compound. RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
This branch of medicine handles more than 100 inflammatory diseases of the bones, muscles, and joints — like lupus and arthritis — and overlaps heavily with immunology. What is it?
Rheumatology: Medical speciality of inflammatory diseases.
Known as 'swede' in British English, this root vegetable is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip — what is it?
Rutabaga: Root vegetable in the Brassica family.
Usually forming an S- or C-shaped curve with a rotational twist, this sideways irregular curvature of the spine sits alongside kyphosis and lordosis among the spine's abnormal curves. What is it?
Scoliosis: Left-right asymmetry of the spine's curvature.
Despite historians noting that email already existed in the early 1970s, this MIT-trained engineer holds a 1982 copyright and claims to have invented it as a teenager — who is he?
Shiva Ayyadurai: American engineer, conspiracy theorist, and entrepreneur.

Self-taught from her father's library and writing to Gauss and Lagrange under a male pseudonym, this French mathematician pioneered elasticity theory and laid groundwork for Fermat's Last Theorem — who was she?
Sophie Germain: French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.

Striking about one in a million people, this rare neurological disorder brings progressive muscular rigidity and spasms that twist the trunk into postural deformities — first described in 1956, what is it?
Stiff-person syndrome: Neurological disorder. The stiffness primarily affects the truncal muscles and is characterised by spasms, resulting in postural deformities.
Its explosive yield became the standard yardstick for comparing bombs and even asteroid impacts; chemists also use it to make charge-transfer salts — what's this nitro compound?
Encompassing everything from storytelling to painting, this broad domain of human creative expression splits into three branches: visual, literary, and performing — what is it called?
The arts: Creative human and cultural expression. The arts, or creative arts, are a vast range of human practices involving creative expression, storytelling, and cultural participation.
Covered in taste buds and divided into oral and pharyngeal parts, this muscular mouth organ also helps clean the teeth and enable speech — what is it?
Tongue: Muscular organ in the mouth of most vertebrates.
Nicknamed the "immortal jellyfish," this tiny sea creature can revert from a sexually mature adult back into an immature, sea-floor-dwelling polyp stage instead of dying — what species is it?
Turritopsis dohrnii: Species of small, biologically immortal jellyfish.

Comprising some 150 to 175 species of shrubs and the occasional small tree, this flowering-plant genus is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but in Africa survives only in the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum: Genus of flowering plants in the moschatel family.
This small insectivorous songbird breeds across Europe, Asia, and North Africa, keeps a rare toehold in western Alaska, and has adapted to hunting bugs in car parks — which bird?
White wagtail: Species of bird. The white wagtail (Motacilla alba) is a small passerine bird in the family Motacillidae, which also includes pipits and longclaws.
Known as courgette in Britain and France, this summer squash is usually picked at 15–25 cm long, though left unharvested it can stretch nearly a meter — what vegetable is it?
Zucchini: Edible summer squash. It is closely related, but not identical, to the marrow; its fruit may be called marrow when mature.
